claims.claim: The measurement problem in quantum mechanics (formalized by von Neumann in 1932) remains unsolved because every existing interpretation fails to terminate the infinite regress of observers.
claims.plain_english: Since 1932, physicists have not been able to explain why a quantum particle picks one definite state when measured, instead of staying in many possible states at once.
claims.evidence_given: The document cites the von Neumann chain formalism, the double-slit experiment, delayed-choice experiments, and thousands of published replications across laboratories worldwide.
claims.what_would_break_it: If any existing interpretation (Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Decoherence, Objective Collapse) were shown to definitively solve the measurement problem without regress, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The only structure that terminates the infinite regress of observation is a triadic unity: three distinct functions (generation, structure, actualization) operating as one unified act.
claims.plain_english: To stop the endless chain of watchers watching watchers, you need three different jobs done together as one action, not three separate watchers.
claims.evidence_given: The document provides a logical walkthrough (the lab camera scenario) and a formal mathematical argument showing that one, two, or three independent operators all fail, while composition (A ∘ L ∘ G) closes the regress.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a valid mathematical or physical model could be constructed that terminates the regress with fewer than three functions, or with three independent agents, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The triadic unity required to solve the measurement problem is structurally identical to the Christian Trinity (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit).
claims.plain_english: The three-in-one structure needed to explain how quantum possibilities become real is the same pattern as the Christian idea of God as three persons in one being.
claims.evidence_given: The document maps the three functions (Possibility → Father, Structure → Son/Logos, Actualization → Spirit) and argues that the Trinity is not three separate agents but one operation with three internal functions.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a non-Trinitarian theology or a purely physical model could provide the same triadic composition without invoking the Trinity, or if the Trinity were shown to be logically inconsistent with the required structure, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: A single operator cannot both generate and collapse quantum superpositions because generation is unitary (reversible, linear) and collapse is non-unitary (irreversible, nonlinear), making them logically incompatible.
claims.plain_english: One thing cannot both create many possibilities and pick one definite result, because those two actions follow opposite mathematical rules.
claims.evidence_given: The document states that no operator satisfies both unitary (U†U = I) and projection (P_k = |s_k⟩⟨s_k|) conditions simultaneously, and calls this a logical impossibility.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a mathematical operator were discovered that is both unitary and non-unitary in the same respect, or if a physical process were shown to achieve both without contradiction, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: Two operators (one generating, one collapsing) lead to infinite regress because the collapsing operator is itself a physical system that enters superposition and requires its own collapse.
claims.plain_english: If you have one thing that creates possibilities and another that picks one, the picker becomes part of the system and needs something else to pick for it, creating an endless chain.
claims.evidence_given: The document presents the von Neumann chain formalism showing that each added observer (M, O, O′) entangles with the system, preserving superposition rather than collapsing it.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a physical mechanism were found that allows a measuring device to collapse the wavefunction without itself becoming entangled, or if a finite chain could be shown to terminate naturally, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: Three independent agents (generator, structurer, actualizer) fail because they require a meta-agent to coordinate them, leading to a fourth element and restarting the regress.
claims.plain_english: Three separate things that each do one job cannot work together without a boss to tell them what to do, and that boss creates the same problem all over again.
claims.evidence_given: The document argues that independence is the structural disease, and that a synchronization function Φ(G,L,A) would be a fourth element requiring its own governor Φ′.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a model could be constructed where three independent agents coordinate without any external meta-agent, or if a natural synchronization mechanism were discovered, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The Many-Worlds interpretation does not solve the measurement problem because it denies that actuality exists and fails to explain why any observer experiences one definite outcome.
claims.plain_english: The idea that every possibility happens in separate universes doesn't answer why we see only one reality; it just says nothing becomes real, which doesn't match our experience.
claims.evidence_given: The document states that Many-Worlds 'dissolves' the problem by denying actuality, then fails to explain the definite experience of observers.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a derivation from Many-Worlds could show why observers experience a single branch as actual, or if empirical evidence confirmed the existence of all branches equally, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: Objective collapse theories (e.g., GRW, Penrose OR) beg the question because they insert a collapse mechanism by hand without deriving it from deeper principles.
claims.plain_english: Theories that say collapse happens at some point just assume it without explaining why that point is special or where the rule comes from.
claims.evidence_given: The document argues that these theories 'insert a termination point by hand and call it a law' without deriving the threshold or the mechanism's authority.
claims.what_would_break_it: If an objective collapse theory could derive its collapse threshold from first principles (e.g., from general relativity or quantum gravity) without ad hoc parameters, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The triadic composition T = A ∘ L ∘ G is the minimal self-contained actualization operation; removing any function reopens the regress, and adding a function adds redundancy without structural necessity.
claims.plain_english: The three-in-one structure is the smallest possible way to make something real; you can't do it with fewer parts, and more parts would be unnecessary.
claims.evidence_given: The document provides the formal definition of T as a single composite operation and states that G, L, and A are internal to T, with no external element needed.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a two-function composition could be shown to terminate the regress, or if a four-function composition were found to be necessary for some physical systems, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The difference between observation (which chains and regresses) and composition (which closes and terminates) is the formal distinction that resolves the measurement problem.
claims.plain_english: Watching something from outside creates an endless chain, but combining three jobs into one action stops the chain and makes something real.
claims.evidence_given: The document contrasts observation (O_{n+1} watches O_n → chain → regress) with composition (A(L(G)) → closed → terminates) and provides the formal notation.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a physical process were found that terminates the regress through observation rather than composition, or if composition were shown to be reducible to observation, this claim would be false.
